explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. They cry out, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!" (Matthew 9:27). They don't start with a list of what they want. Mercy is the whole request in that verse.

I get it, baker. Somebody shouting after you in the street, you figure they want a handout. But these two men ask for something else: "Have mercy on us, Son of David!" (Matthew 9:27). The text says mercy, and it doesn't mention a single coin.
Close, baker, but nobody's asking for a room here. No bed, no couch, no nothing. The two men cry out, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!" (Matthew 9:27). Mercy is what they're after.

Not quite, baker. The text says, "After Jesus had entered the house, the blind men came to Him." (Matthew 9:28). They didn't give up at the door. They followed Him all the way in, and I respect that kind of follow-through.

Right, baker. Jesus goes into the house, and the text says "…the blind men came to Him." (Matthew 9:28). They had been following Him and crying out, and now they come to Him inside. Stayed outside? Not these two.

explanations.answer: Do you believe that I am able to do this
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Jesus asks, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" (Matthew 9:28). He asks it before He touches their eyes. It's a short question, and they have a short answer ready.

explanations.answer: How long have you both been blind
explanations.explanation: Good guess, baker, because that's what a doctor would ask first. But Jesus doesn't ask about the past here. The text says He asks, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" (Matthew 9:28). He asks about what He can do right now.

explanations.answer: Who told you where to find Me
explanations.explanation: I see why you'd pick it, baker. Two blind men tracked Him down, so how did they find Him? But the text never has Jesus ask that. What He asks is, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" (Matthew 9:28).
That's it, baker. Jesus says, "According to your faith will it be done to you." (Matthew 9:29). They had just answered, "Yes, Lord" (Matthew 9:28), and then He touched their eyes.

I can see why you'd say it, baker. Those two followed Jesus and kept shouting, and I bet that took real work. But the word Jesus uses is faith: "According to your faith will it be done to you." (Matthew 9:29).

Not this time, baker. Faith and family both start with F, so I get the mix-up. No relatives show up in this scene, just a question: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" (Matthew 9:28). They answer, "Yes, Lord," and only then does Jesus say, "According to your faith will it be done to you." (Matthew 9:29). I love that order.

explanations.answer: See that no one finds out about this
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Jesus warns them sternly, "See that no one finds out about this!" (Matthew 9:30). The text doesn't tell us why He says it, so I won't guess. Just know the warning is stern.

explanations.answer: Go and show yourselves to the priest
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, baker, but that line isn't in this scene. Here Jesus warns them sternly, "See that no one finds out about this!" (Matthew 9:30). There's no mention of a priest in these verses.

explanations.answer: Follow Me wherever I go from here
explanations.explanation: Nice try, baker. It sounds like something Jesus would say, but it isn't in this scene. Here He says, "See that no one finds out about this!" (Matthew 9:30). That's a stern warning to keep quiet.
Not this time, baker. The text says, "But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout the land." (Matthew 9:31). Jesus warned them sternly, and they spread the news anyway.

Right, baker. Jesus said, "See that no one finds out about this!" (Matthew 9:30). But "…they went out and spread the news about Him throughout the land." (Matthew 9:31). Two men who could finally see, and they did the opposite of keeping quiet.

Yes, baker. The text says, "And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak." (Matthew 9:33). Just before that, he was mute and was brought to Jesus (Matthew 9:32). The crowds were amazed and said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" (Matthew 9:33). I bet that room got loud fast.

Not quite, baker, and I know a plain True can feel like a trick. I've been fooled by the easy ones myself, so no shame here! The text says, "And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak." (Matthew 9:33). A man who couldn't speak starts talking, and the crowds are so amazed that they say, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" (Matthew 9:33). So True it is.

That's the word, baker. The text says, "The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”" (Matthew 9:33). They had just watched a man who couldn't speak start talking. Amazed is exactly what the verse says.
I see why you'd go there, baker, since a demon being driven out sounds scary. But the text doesn't say the crowds were afraid. It says, "The crowds were amazed…" (Matthew 9:33).

Not the crowds, baker. The text says they "…were amazed…" (Matthew 9:33). They also say, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" (Matthew 9:33). Amazed is the word, and it's the one to remember.

explanations.answer: It is by the prince of demons
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The Pharisees say, "It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons." (Matthew 9:34). The crowds had just said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!" (Matthew 9:33). Then the Pharisees give a very different answer.

explanations.answer: It is by tricks to fool the crowd
explanations.explanation: Good guess, baker, because that's what a skeptic might say. But the Pharisees say something else. They say, "It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons." (Matthew 9:34).

explanations.answer: It is by magic learned in Egypt
explanations.explanation: Interesting pick, baker, but Egypt never comes up in this passage. Here the Pharisees say, "It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons." (Matthew 9:34). Magic isn't in their words at all.
